site.home.description: CDelivery is a self-hosted operations platform for deploying applications, managing domains and TLS, scheduling jobs, and viewing logs and metrics.
site.safety.title: Operate and release with confidence
site.safety.operationsBody: CDelivery regularly checks that your app is online and that users can complete tasks like signing in.
site.safety.releasesBody: During an update, CDelivery starts an instance of the new version in the same production environment. Only health checks reach this instance. The current version keeps serving users. The rollout begins when the checks pass. A failed check blocks the release.
site.safety.dependencyTitle: Verify app updates with connected apps
site.safety.dependencyBody: When one app calls another, CDelivery checks that they still work together when either app is updated. If a health check fails for either app, the release is blocked and the current version keeps serving users.
site.safety.databaseTitle: Verify database changes with your apps
site.safety.databaseBody: CDelivery creates a temporary branch of the production database and applies the change there. It connects a preview instance of each dependent app to the branch and runs that app’s health checks. Live apps keep using the production database. CDelivery applies the same change there only after all checks pass.
site.safety.dependencyDiagram: App A calls B v1 to serve live requests. In the same production environment, XHealth tests a preview of A that calls B v2. The check fails, so CDelivery blocks the release of B v2.
site.safety.databaseDiagram: The live app serves users from the production database. In the same production environment, XHealth tests a preview of the app against a temporary branch with the SQL change already applied. The app check fails, so CDelivery blocks the change to the production database.
site.observability.title: Observability costs as low as 1% of Datadog’s
site.observability.intro: Ready out of the box. No SDK needed. Automatically collect server and app metrics and logs, with long-term storage on disk or object stores like S3. New data can be ready to query and analyze in as little as 3 seconds.
site.observability.costTitle: Low costs, more for what matters
site.observability.costBody: 1 GB of logs a day. 365 GB a year. Just $7.23 for the first year.
site.observability.performanceBody:
Measured throughput of {{throughput}} MB/s, with peak memory usage of just {{memory}} GiB.
Multiple instances and high availability help you keep up as your user base and data grow.
site.observability.chartDescription: Log ingestion throughput: {{throughput}} MB/s. Peak server memory: {{memory}} MiB. {{indexes}} indexes on an {{cores}}-core AWS EC2 {{instance}}.
site.observability.periodTotal: Estimated total for the first {{months}} months (USD)

site.observability.noScript: Enable JavaScript to adjust this estimate. Default costs are shown below.
site.observability.storageFees: The CDelivery estimate includes compressed S3 Standard storage in US East (N. Virginia), using monthly averages and tiered rates of $0.021–$0.023/GiB/month, plus one PUT per 16 MB at $0.005 per 1,000 requests.
site.observability.datadogFees: Datadog uses annual-plan rates: $0.10/GB ingested. For one month, Standard at $2.50/million indexed logs with 30-day retention; longer periods use Flex Starter at $0.60/million stored logs/month, based on monthly averages.
site.observability.flexLimits: Flex supports 3, 6, 12 or 15 months, fewer than 2 billion logs ingested per month and up to 10 billion stored. Other settings are extrapolated. Estimates exclude servers, reads, transfer, taxes, discounts and free allowances.
site.observability.assumptions: Estimates cover the selected retention period, starting from empty storage with steady ingestion. One month = 365/12 days; input units are decimal and S3 storage uses GiB.
site.observability.metricsCost: Metrics for one server or app: just $0.6758 a year.
site.gateway.title:
High-performance gateway.
Less hassle. Lower costs
site.gateway.intro: CDelivery builds its reverse proxy gateway on Cloudflare’s {{pingora}}. Proven at scale on Cloudflare’s network, Pingora provides a mature, stable, and reliable foundation.
site.gateway.operations: Ready out of the box, with multiple instances for high availability and automatic HTTPS certificate management for both single-instance and multi-instance deployments.
site.xconfig.title: Build and run highly available apps that scale with ease
site.xconfig.description: Distribute configuration to multiple service instances with the same ease as local development, without learning a new stack or integrating an SDK. Run multiple instances and scale out easily, without a separate configuration service to maintain. With XHealth, services using a new configuration pass checks before going live. Scale from your first user to millions.
site.xconfig.diagramDescription: XConfig distributes the same app.conf configuration to three application instances. Version v2 is an illustrative label.
site.ai.title: AI diagnostics, proactive monitoring
site.ai.context: CDelivery brings together runtime metrics, application logs, access records, and operation events, giving AI the context to analyze issues and assist with diagnosis. It includes an AI assistant and supports connecting your preferred AI tools through MCP and API access.
site.ai.duty: With AI on-call enabled, CDelivery runs ongoing checks and steps in right away when an anomaly strikes—investigating the cause and impact, taking initial action within the permissions you grant, and sharing findings and progress according to your policy. You don’t have to stay in front of a screen—rest easy late at night or while you’re away.
site.ai.diagramDescription: Metrics, application logs, access records and operation events are examples of the context available to AI analysis. Outputs include diagnoses, actions and notifications.
site.ai.channels: Receive notifications, continue conversations, request actions, and check results through familiar channels like email and Slack. The web interface is mobile-friendly too. Get things done, wherever you are.

site.openSource.description:

site.footprint.title: Small footprint. More room for your apps
site.footprint.description: Low CPU and memory overhead across deployment management, the gateway, and observability. CDelivery requires only Docker, with no additional services such as PostgreSQL, and supports automatic failover within the cluster.
site.footprint.codeDescription: Across the core service, gateway, observability, agents, and shared libraries.

site.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
site.faq.capacity.question: How many servers can CDelivery support?
site.faq.capacity.answer: You can start with just 1 server. CDelivery itself does not impose a limit on the number of servers. A single cluster can scale to 5,000 servers, comparable to the node count officially supported by Kubernetes.
site.faq.kubernetes.question: Why choose CDelivery over Kubernetes?
site.faq.kubernetes.answer: Because your team’s time and energy are better spent on your product. CDelivery brings application deployment, HTTPS, logs and metrics, business workflow checks, and release validation together in one platform, reducing the work of choosing tools, integrating components, and keeping everything running. Start with a single server and expand to multiple nodes as your business grows, without dedicated Kubernetes operations staff. Safer deployments. Simpler operations.

site.autoscaling.title: Automatic replica scaling
site.autoscaling.description: Automatically add or remove application replicas within your configured range based on CPU load. Scale up when load rises and scale down after sustained low load, adapting resource use to your app’s needs.
site.autoscaling.diagramDescription: Illustrative timeline: high CPU utilization triggers scaling from two to four replicas, followed by a drop in CPU utilization. After sustained low CPU utilization, replicas scale down to two and CPU utilization rises again.

site.comparison.title: Where CDelivery is genuinely different
site.comparison.intro: Running containers, reverse proxying, single-node HTTPS, and basic restarts—every tool here has those, so they aren’t listed below. What’s below is where your choice actually changes reliability and effort.
site.comparison.rows.workflow.title: Avoid “worked in staging, broke in prod”
site.comparison.rows.workflow.lightweigh: Usually check only process or port liveness; traffic switches without verifying workflows.
site.comparison.rows.workflow.kubernetes: Native probes check basic health; isolated production and caller checks need custom pipelines.
site.comparison.rows.workflow.cdelivery: Runs an isolated preview instance in real production—no live traffic—and validates callers together before rollout.
site.comparison.rows.database.title: Rehearse database changes on real data
site.comparison.rows.database.lightweigh: Not included. Teams typically back up and run changes directly on production.
site.comparison.rows.database.kubernetes: Orchestrates containers only; branching real production data needs extra tools and scripts.
site.comparison.rows.database.cdelivery: Quickly forks the production DB to a temporary branch (CDelivery-deployed, Neon, and PlanetScale) and validates dependent apps before applying.
site.comparison.rows.observability.title: Observability cost and upkeep
site.comparison.rows.observability.light: Usually live container logs only; long-term search and metrics mean maintaining extra tools or buying SaaS—expensive in both effort and cost.
site.comparison.rows.observability.kuber: Self-hosting HA Prometheus and Loki/ELK carries heavy staffing and resource costs; SaaS like Datadog brings sky-high bills.
site.comparison.rows.observability.cdeli: Built-in Insight with no SDK or separate cluster, plus free distributed multi-instance HA; queryable in as little as 3s, down to 1% of Datadog’s cost.
site.comparison.rows.ha.title: Multi-node HA and seamless upgrades
site.comparison.rows.ha.lightweight: Built mainly for single nodes or small setups; distributed HA often requires maintaining extra products or paying for add-ons.
site.comparison.rows.ha.kubernetes: Combining components such as Traefik and Argo makes upgrades risky. Some commercial gateways charge extra for distributed features.
site.comparison.rows.ha.cdelivery: Scales from 1 to 5,000 servers; includes free multi-instance HA, rolling upgrades, and automatic multi-node HTTPS certificate sync.
site.comparison.rows.footprint.title: Platform dependencies and footprint
site.comparison.rows.footprint.lightweig: Often bundles a database or cache; adding config, jobs, and observability stacks up components.
site.comparison.rows.footprint.kubernete: Control plane, etcd, and add-ons are heavy—often taking gigabytes of RAM and steady ops effort.
site.comparison.rows.footprint.cdelivery: Requires only Docker, with built-in XConfig, Secrets, and XJob—starting at ~160 MiB across core, gateway, and Insight.
site.comparison.rows.ai.title: AI on-call with full context
site.comparison.rows.ai.lightweight: Lacks long-term metrics, historical context, ongoing memory, and active on-call; troubleshooting means pasting snippets to AI with no closed-loop action.
site.comparison.rows.ai.kubernetes: Observability, gateway, and orchestration stay siloed; wiring in AI often leaves you with data but no actions—or actions without context—with weak cross-tool integration.
site.comparison.rows.ai.cdelivery: Unifies long-term metrics, logs, access, and events natively; AI sees the full picture, patrols proactively, acts within role permissions, and exposes MCP/API.
site.comparison.rows.ownership.title: Data ownership and software cost
site.comparison.rows.ownership.lightweig: Data stays on your servers with no per-seat fees—they get this part right.
site.comparison.rows.ownership.kubernete: Fully open source on your infrastructure—Kubernetes gets this right, with cost mainly in ops staffing.
site.comparison.rows.ownership.cdelivery: Apache License 2.0, free for commercial use, no per-seat pricing, and 100% of data stays on your servers.
site.comparison.footnote: This comparison reflects the typical out-of-the-box experience of each approach rather than a specific product. Many of these capabilities can be built with extra tools, custom pipelines, or paid plans.
